text: Attempt 11: attempt 10's audited layout built up front (blocks 1+2 on day one), pace check enforces the target curve, debt capped at 1 + population/8,000 loans, taxes 4/4/4, seaport at ~5,000, zoo ~10,000.
Loan #1 ($10,000). A second loan was refused: the game says the credit rating must improve first. Taxes 4/4/4.
Day one ($15,764): road + rail links, coal plant, fire stations x2, 288 light home tiles, shops, factories, 12 riverbank pumps, pipes. Build check and audit passed.

Attempt 10 missed (14,190 in 2018). The reflection over all ten attempts says land early is the strongest lever, so attempt 11 starts with 288 home tiles instead of 108. Learned today: the game refuses a second loan at founding (credit rating), so day one is capped at about $20,000.
Factory tax 4 -> 3 (jobs first: home demand at max, 261 empty home tiles, factories lead a small city).

Pace alarm, Feb 2001: 480 people vs 2,200 target. Land is not the problem (261 empty home tiles); the first year is slow because jobs come first. Cut factory tax to 3 and run on; next block when the credit rating allows a second loan.
Loan #2 ($10,000): the credit rating now allows it (refused in 2000).
2003 plan ($8,649): attempt 10's block 3 (east homes, shops, factory strip) and block 4 (south district, 264 home tiles). Home tiles zoned: 683 (pace target 672).

Audit stopped the clock: block 4's power column had a one-tile gap at (77,56) (attempt 10 fed it from the west plant, left out here) and the y38 water main was not joined. Fixed. Build check also caught one home tile at (87,40) that lost its zone during the fix and restored it.

Feb 2003: 2,970 people, behind the population pace (7,200) but land is now ahead: 683 home tiles zoned. Growth has been ~1,500 a year with land to spare, so the speed of building is the limit now, not land.

Power + water shortage (spare 4%/0%, 30 buildings unpowered): gas plant ($2,000; cash was $3,754, coal costs $4,000) on the river strip, joined via a new line column x75 and the crossing at (76,47); 5 riverbank pumps. Total $2,630.
Shop and factory tax 4 -> 6 (both demands at maximum; homes stay 4 - rule: homes last).
Loan #3 ($10,000), slightly ahead of the debt rule (max 2 until 8,000 people): city at 6,930, growing ~2,500 a year, out of power and water.
Coal plant next to the gas plant ($4,000) + 19 north riverbank pumps (attempt 9's plan).

Control: the camera calibration clicked a lake-shore tile and the game built a 3-tile bridge (95-97,18). Build guard caught the stray road; the bridge was bulldozed. autocal.sh now checks 24 px around each spot for water and stops with an alarm if any new bridge tile appears.

Loan #4 ($10,000): land full (21 empty home tiles), all demand at max for 2 years. Rule changed from '1 + pop/8,000' to payback: a loan must buy land for 5,500+ people (~250 home tiles + jobs). Taxes 5/7/7 (homes +1, shops/factories +1).
District 5 south of road y76 ($9,072 with a third coal plant): 252 home tiles, 72 shop, 72 factory, fire station, pipes. River cut the west road at y90 (plan changed by the water preflight).

Dec 2006: 11,520 people, the second-best start of all attempts (attempt 4: 14,040). Every block filled within ~2 years. The money problem is back (cash $1,987 before the loan): at 4-6% tax, tax income is below loan payments, so the plan is to keep growth outrunning debt.
Loan #5 ($10,000): home demand falling toward the ~15,000 cap (847), land nearly full; buys the first zoo + district 6 (land for ~4,000 people).
District 6 east of road x108 ($5,900): zoo ($3,000), 162 home tiles, 72 shop tiles, power via 4 crossings over road x108 and a line row y56, pipes.
16 riverbank pumps rows 77-92 on a new line column x75 ($2,019): water spare was 0-6% for 18 months (146 dry buildings). Joined district 6's y66 pipe (it touched the network only diagonally).
Control: play.sh only printed WARN lines for low water, so the loop ran 18 months short of water. play.sh now stops when spare water or power is under 10%.

Dec 2010: 16,270 people (attempt 4 had 21,120, attempt 10 had 11,220). Home demand turned negative near 16,000 even with the zoo; part of the cause may be the long water shortage, now fixed. Cash $1,000 after pumps; 5 loans.
Loan #6 ($10,000). Factory tax 7 -> 9 (factory demand at maximum for 8 years).

West factory strip x54-74 y64-75 (196 tiles, $1,732): there was ZERO empty factory land while factory demand sat at max, unemployment 10%, 162 abandoned homes. Fourth coal plant ($4,000): spare power 18%.

Feb 2012: the stall at 16,000 looks like the same one attempts 4, 6 and 10 hit, but the save shows why: no empty factory land at all (homes 1,112 tiles vs factories 489), so the unemployed left. Attempt 10's 'industry cap' reading was probably wrong too. Cash went negative (-$1,199) before loan #6.
Loan #7 ($10,000), over the 6-loan limit on purpose: the seaport test decides attempt 12's plan.

First seaport ($3,160, 22 tiles) on the river bank west of the plants: factory demand at max for 2 years with 137 empty factory tiles and 15% unemployment = the industry cap; the rail link alone is not enough.

Feb 2014: stuck at 16,000 for 3 years. 137 empty factory tiles do not fill while factory demand reads maximum, so this is the game's industry cap. Testing a seaport now; if factories start filling, the next strategy builds it in the first years.
Seaport result: factories 524 -> 606 built and unemployment 15% -> 9% within 18 months - the seaport lifts the factory cap. Added 108 factory tiles below road y97 ($1,190).
Feb 2016: 17,970 people. The seaport experiment worked: factory land filled again as soon as it existed. Lesson for the next attempt: seaport in the first years, not at 16,000.
